verdict.rationale: Highnote's own spend rules evaluate authorizations and can permit or restrict transactions by merchant category code. Its marketing also states that merchant category restrictions are evaluated at authorization, before funds move, at the card, account, or program level. Single-merchant locks are not documented, and collaborative authorization is only a developer building block for custom logic, so it earns no credit. missing for 10: documented single-merchant (merchant ID) lock capability, explicit allowlist vs blocklist configuration details, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can restrict where a card works — merchant category (MCC) allowlists and blocklists, and single-merchant locks — applied at authorization time

citations.quote: Spend rules let you automate logic on authorizations that permit or restrict transactions. You can configure that logic on merchant category codes (MCC), dollar amount, authorization count, and more.
Set velocity limits, merchant category restrictions, and per-transaction caps at the card, account, or program level. Every rule is evaluated at authorization, before funds move.
